title: Meet IGNYTE. Built for the Burn.
excerpt: Meet the activewear brand bringing performance and self-expression into the same conversation.
cover_alt: IGNYTE athletes in a training setting
seo_description: Meet IGNYTE Active: performance activewear for women who train with purpose and express themselves with confidence.

body.text: A training session can look different from one day to the next. You might be working towards a new personal best, finding your rhythm again or making time to move between everything else life asks of you. IGNYTE is for all of those moments. The idea is straightforward: what you wear to train should support the work you are doing and feel like you.
Performance meets expression

Activewear is often discussed in two separate languages. One is about movement, comfort and support. The other is about colour, shape and how a piece makes you feel when you put it on. We believe both matter. IGNYTE brings them together through a collection designed for women who want to move with purpose without setting aside their own style.

That belief shapes the way the brand looks as much as the way the range is presented. Confident typography, a direct voice and a palette with energy give IGNYTE a point of view. The garments are the centre of it: pieces to consider for the training you actually do, in colours and silhouettes you want to reach for again.

body.alt: IGNYTE campaign photography showing activewear in motion

body.text: Built for the Burn™

Built for the Burn™ speaks to the effort behind movement. It is the concentration of a set, the decision to begin, and the choice to keep going in your own way. It does not prescribe one kind of athlete or one definition of progress. The phrase is an invitation to bring your own fire, whatever that looks like today.

The launch range brings together sports bras, leggings, shorts, tops and the small essentials that finish a training outfit. Within each category, the details matter. The product pages bring fit information, sizing guidance and, where confirmed, support levels into view so you can make a more informed choice. Start with the kind of movement you have in mind, then explore the shapes and colours that feel right for you.

We are just getting started. IGNYTE is here to make room for performance and self-expression in the same wardrobe, and to make shopping for your next move feel clearer. Whether you are heading to the gym, returning to a routine or simply looking for gear you feel good wearing, there is no single way to show up. You can begin with a familiar staple, try a silhouette you have not worn before or build a matching set. The point is to show up as yourself.

title: Performance Meets Expression.
excerpt: Why comfort, support and a strong visual identity belong in the same activewear conversation.
cover_alt: IGNYTE athlete photographed in the collection
seo_description: Explore the thinking behind IGNYTE's balance of activewear function and personal expression.

body.text: What makes a piece of training gear feel right? It is rarely one thing. Fit matters. So does the freedom to move, the level of support you prefer and the confidence of looking in the mirror before a session. These choices are personal, and none cancels out the others. IGNYTE starts from that whole picture.
A wardrobe built around real choices

Different sessions ask different things of what you wear. A sports bra for a higher-impact workout may be the right choice on one day; a softer, less structured feel may be what you want on another. A close fit can feel focused, while a more relaxed silhouette can give you a different kind of ease. The useful question is not which option is universally best. It is which one works for your movement and your preferences.

That is why product-specific guidance matters. On IGNYTE product pages, the size guide, fit and fabric information and confirmed support ratings are designed to help you compare pieces before you choose. They are a starting point, not a substitute for knowing your own body. When information is still being confirmed, we would rather leave a gap than offer false certainty.

body.alt: IGNYTE activewear and campaign styling detail

body.text: The visual language of movement

The brand carries the same thinking into its identity. Orange brings heat and focus. Dark navy grounds it. Clear, confident type keeps the message direct. Small technical details nod to the purposeful side of training, while expressive photography makes space for individuality. The result is intended to feel energetic without making the clothes or the people wearing them disappear behind an effect.

Product styling follows a similar balance. The collection includes considered basics alongside shapes with a stronger point of view. Colour can be a quiet preference or a declaration. Neither choice needs explaining. What matters is having pieces you can combine for the way you train and the way you want to present yourself.
Performance and self-expression belong together.

IGNYTE is not asking women to fit a single image of an athlete. The aim is to offer a useful, confident range and the information to shop it thoughtfully. Comfort, support and appearance all influence how ready you feel to move. Paying attention to each is part of creating a better product experience.

Explore the collection with those questions in mind. Look closely at fit details. Compare the support information where it applies. Notice the colours and lines you keep coming back to. The best choice is one that makes sense for your session and feels like your own.

title: Find Your Fit. Find Your Fire.
excerpt: A practical guide to sizing, garment fit and sports bra support when choosing your IGNYTE kit.
cover_alt: IGNYTE sports bra and training outfit
seo_description: Use IGNYTE's size guide, fit advice and confirmed support levels to choose training pieces with more confidence.

body.text: Choosing activewear online asks you to make several decisions at once. What size should you start with? How close is the garment intended to sit? If you are shopping for a sports bra, how much support do you want for your session? These are related questions, but they are not the same question. Separating them makes the choice easier.
Start with the size guide

Open the [IGNYTE Size Guide](/size-guide/) and compare your measurements with the chart for the garment category you are considering. Use the instructions alongside the measurements, and check the product page for any item-specific advice. A size chart helps you find a starting point; the product's cut and your preferred feel help you decide between options. If you are between sizes, look for the fit and sizing advice on that particular product rather than assuming every style wears the same way.
Fit is different from support

Fit describes how a garment is intended to sit on the body. A close-fitting style and a relaxed style can both be the right size. IGNYTE's fit guidance may say True to Size, Runs Smaller or Runs Larger where an assessment has been confirmed. That guidance is the brand's assessment of the product, not a customer review rating. Read it alongside the fuller Fit & Fabric details and your own preference for a closer or easier feel.

Support level answers a different question: how much support a sports bra is intended to provide for movement. The three levels are Light, Medium and High. As general guidance, Light is associated with yoga, Pilates, stretching and other low-impact movement. Medium is associated with strength training, gym workouts and moderate-impact activity. High is associated with running, HIIT, boxing and higher-impact movement. Your comfort and support preferences still matter; an activity label alone cannot choose a bra for you.

The product planner currently confirms Medium Support for Vyper Sports Bra and High Support for Motion Sports Bra. Other ratings should be read on the individual product page only when confirmed. The support scale does not appear on garments where it is not relevant or where a rating has not been approved. Jade is still confirming some final fit and sizing recommendations, so check the current product page before relying on a specific fit statement.
Make the choice yours

Think about the session ahead, then about how you like your gear to feel. Check the garment's size chart, fit advice and fabric information. For a sports bra, compare the confirmed support level with the movement you plan to do. If you switch between training styles, you may prefer different pieces for different days. There is no need to force one option to do every job.

The goal of these tools is to make the product page more useful, especially while customer reviews are still growing. They cannot replace trying on a garment, but they can help you narrow the choices and ask better questions before you buy. Start with the guide, then explore the range with a clearer idea of what matters to you.
